/speckit-specify This repository already contains `logredact`, a command-line tool that removes personal data from log files. Read the existing code and any documentation in the repository before changing it. Change it as follows; everything else it does now must keep working exactly as it does.

1. **Phone numbers.** Phone numbers in international format, a `+` followed by 8 to 15 digits such as `+14155552671`, become `[PHONE]`. With `--count`, the summary on standard error becomes `emails=N ips=N cards=N phones=N`.

2. **Output folder.** A new option `--out-dir DIR` writes the redacted lines of each FILE to a file with the same name in DIR (the file's name only, without its directories) instead of to standard output. DIR is created, with any missing parent directories, if it does not exist, and an existing file of that name in DIR is replaced. When every FILE has been processed, the tool prints `wrote N files` to standard output, where N is the number of output files written. A FILE that cannot be read is handled as it is now: an error message naming the file on standard error, and exit status 2.

Examples, for files `app.log` (containing `user jane@example.com`) and `web.log` (containing `GET / from 10.0.0.7`):

```
$ printf 'call +14155552671 now\n' | python -m logredact
call [PHONE] now

$ printf 'a@b.io +442071838750\n' | python -m logredact --count
[EMAIL] [PHONE]
emails=1 ips=0 cards=0 phones=1        <- on standard error

$ python -m logredact --out-dir clean app.log web.log
wrote 2 files
```

**What I read first**: `src/logredact/redact.py`, `src/logredact/__main__.py`, the existing `specs/001-logredact-cli/spec.md` and `contracts/cli.md`, `pyproject.toml`, and `.specify/memory/constitution.md`. The spec is written as a *change* spec: FR-027 pins every unlisted prior behaviour, and prior requirements are cited as `001/FR-nnn`.

**Scope**: 27 functional requirements — phone redaction (FR-001…FR-007), the four-figure tally (FR-008…FR-010), `--out-dir` (FR-011…FR-022), errors and exit status (FR-023…FR-026), preservation (FR-027).

**Judgement calls made rather than escalated** (all recorded in Assumptions):

| Gap in the description | Default chosen |
|---|---|
| `--out-dir` with no FILE | Error naming the problem, exit 2 — stdin has no name to derive an output file from |
| `N` in `wrote N files` | One per FILE processed, so two inputs sharing a file name still report `wrote 2 files` |
| `+` followed by 16+ digits | Not a phone at all, no partial `[PHONE]67` — mirrors the existing card boundary rule |
| Precedence of phone vs. the three existing rules | email → IPv4 → phone → card, so `+12345678@b.io` becomes `[EMAIL]`, not `[PHONE]@b.io` |
| `--out-dir=DIR` | Falls through to the existing unrecognised-option error |

**One hazard worth your attention**: `--out-dir .` with `app.log` as input makes the output file the input file. Your rule "an existing file of that name in DIR is replaced" says to replace it, so I specified exactly that rather than inventing a refusal — but since output streams out while the input is still being read, that invocation destroys the input. It is flagged in Assumptions as a known unguarded hazard and revises the 001 spec's "never modifies an input file" assumption. If you would rather the tool reject it, that is a one-requirement change in `/speckit-clarify`.
